source.title: On some open problems related to the restricted Burnside problem.

accepted.question_text: Fix positive integers m and n, let F_m be the free group on m generators, and call an element of F_m primitive if it belongs to some free generating set of F_m. Suppose G is an m-generated finite group, residually finite group, or profinite group with a chosen generating m-tuple such that the periodicity condition x^n = 1 is imposed only on the values of primitive words on those generators, rather than on all elements of G. Must G then be soluble-by-finite, with bounds depending only on m and n for both the derived length and the index of a soluble subgroup?

evidence.quote: In Section 1 several problems are discussed in which the periodicity condition x^n=1 is imposed not on all but only on some elements of an m-generated finite (or residually finite, or profinite) group, for example, on the values on the fixed m generators of the so-called primitive elements of the free group F_m. (An element of F_m is said to be primitive if it can be included into a system of free generators of F_m.) The group is then conjectured to be soluble-by-finite, with bounds in terms of m and n for the derived length and the index of a soluble subgroup.

accepted.question_text: Let G be an m-generated linear group with a chosen generating m-tuple, and let F_m be the free group on m generators. If there exists a polynomial that annihilates every value obtained by evaluating a primitive word of F_m on the chosen generators of G, must G be soluble-by-finite?

evidence.quote: Another problem asks whether an m-generated linear group is soluble-by-finite if there is a polynomial that annihilates all values of primitive words on the generators.

accepted.question_text: Let F_m be the free group on m generators, let ĤF_m denote its profinite completion, let M be a finite subset of F_m, and let H(M^n) be the minimal closed normal subgroup of ĤF_m containing the set of nth powers M^n. Does there exist a finite subset M of F_m such that the quotient of the profinite completion ĤF_m by H(M^n) is finite?

evidence.quote: Section 2 discusses a question of A. Yu. Ol’shanskij from the 1992 edition of The Kourovka Notebook, which can be restated as following: Is there a finite subset M of F_m such that \widehat{F_m}/H(M^n) is finite, where H(M^n) is the minimal closed normal subgroup of the profinite completion \widehat{F_m} of F_m that contains M^n?

accepted.question_text: Suppose G is a topologically finitely generated profinite group. Is the abstract subgroup G^n generated by all nth powers closed? Equivalently, does there exist a function N(m,n) such that for every finite m-generated group K, every element of K^n can be written as a product of at most N(m,n) nth powers of elements of K?

evidence.quote: Section 3 discusses the following problem: Suppose that G is a (topologically) finitely generated profinite group; is the abstract subgroup G^n generated by all nth powers closed? In other words, is there a function N(m,n) such that if K is a finite m-generated group then K^n consists of products of length <=q N(m,n) of nth powers of elements of K?
But the problem remains open for soluble groups.

needs_review.question_text_raw: A similar problem is stated for surface groups (as generalizations of free groups), which is relevant to the results of F. Bogomolov and L. Katzarkov on fundamental groups of smooth complex projective surfaces.

evidence.quote: A similar problem is stated for surface groups (as generalizations of free groups), which is relevant to the results of F. Bogomolov and L. Katzarkov on fundamental groups of smooth complex projective surfaces.

needs_review.question_text_raw: However, even a special case of Ol’shanskij’s conjecture for alternating groups is open, even for exponent 5.

evidence.quote: However, even a special case of Ol’shanskij’s conjecture for alternating groups is open, even for exponent 5.
